sections.heading: C — Before You Drive
sections.markdown:
## C — Before You Drive

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A39
Sit upright with your back against the seat and your feet on the floor. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A39
Set the seat and mirrors for a clear surrounding view, easy pedal access and a comfortable steering reach with airbag space. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A39
Raise the seat enough to see the road, using a cushion if needed, without moving so far forward that steering is hindered. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A39
You should be able to switch between brake and accelerator easily while your heel stays on the floor. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A39
Position the steering-wheel top no higher than your shoulders and below your chin. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A39
Leave 10 inches between your chest and the steering wheel for the airbag, and avoid reclining the seatback. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A39
The head restraint should touch the back of your head above ear level. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A39
Set the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A39
Set a day-night mirror for the current light conditions to reduce glare from following headlights. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A39
Adjust rearview and side mirrors before starting to drive. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A40
To set the left exterior mirror, rest your head against the closed left window and adjust until only a small part of the vehicle’s left rear edge is visible. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A40
To set the right exterior mirror, lean right with your head directly below the inside rearview mirror and adjust until the right vehicle side is barely visible. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A40
Exterior mirrors should provide the widest useful view to the sides and rear. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A40
Fasten your safety belt, and ensure occupants use belts or appropriate child seats. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A40
Belts reduce crash injury and death and help prevent occupants from being thrown out. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A40
Belts help keep the driver behind the wheel during sudden stops or turns so control can be maintained. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A40
In a collision an unbelted occupant keeps moving until striking something inside the stopped vehicle. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A40
Belts help resist slouching and reduce the effort of remaining in the seat as the vehicle bounces or turns. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A41
Buckle before starting the car because an emergency leaves no time to fasten the belt. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A41
Wear the shoulder belt across your shoulder and chest, never beneath an arm or behind the back. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A41
Wear the lap belt comfortably tight below the stomach and over the hips and hip bones. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A41
Airbags provide added protection and work with safety belts; they do not replace wearing a belt. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A41
Airbags and belts help prevent the head and upper body from striking the wheel or dashboard. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A41
Consult the owner’s manual for information specific to the vehicle’s airbags. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

Misconceptions: airbags supplement belts instead of replacing them. [A41]
Mnemonic: position, mirrors, belts, child restraints.
Glossary: the lap belt rests below the stomach over the hip bones. [A41]
Dynamic facts: statistics and conflicting child-restraint boundary wording remain verification debt.

sections.heading: C2 — Before You Drive
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Before You Drive

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A42
The rear seat is the safest riding position for a child of any age. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A42
Never install a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A42
Follow both the vehicle manual and child-restraint instructions, secure the seat correctly and buckle the child into it. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A42
The manual advises rear-facing travel in the back seat for children younger than 2. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A42
An unrestrained occupant can be injured or killed by an airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A42
An infant must not ride in the front seat of a vehicle fitted with a passenger-side airbag. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A42
Drivers and front passengers should sit as far from the wheel or dashboard as possible, especially if short, pregnant or elderly. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A42
A child safety seat is defined as one meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A42
The defined federally approved child-restraint system elevates a child for correct use of a lap-and-shoulder belt and meets Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A42
In a vehicle federally required to have safety belts, the operator must secure a child weighing less than 55 pounds in a child safety seat. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A43
The operator must secure a child younger than 8 who weighs at least 55 but less than 80 pounds in a federally approved child-restraint system. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A43
A passenger younger than 18 must use a seat belt when older than 8 or taller than 4 feet 9 inches, unless a child seat or child-restraint system is still required. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A43
A passenger aged 18 or older must be properly belted in a vehicle federally required to have seat belts. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A43
The operator of a vehicle federally required to have seat belts must wear the operator’s own belt, subject to the stated exceptions. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A43
A United States Postal Service rural carrier is exempt from belt use while delivering mail. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A43
A taxi or limousine operator is not responsible for fastening the belt of a fare-paying passenger. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A43
A newspaper deliverer is exempt from belt use during actual delivery or duties requiring frequent vehicle entry and exit. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

sections.heading: D — Before You Drive
sections.markdown:
## D — Before You Drive
Accuracy scope: Before You Drive facts use the pinned official PDF and one physical page per fact; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
Uncontextualized survival multipliers, injury-risk percentages, fatality totals and belt-use prevalence are withheld as dated-statistic debt; no present-day population estimate is inferred. [A40] [A41]
The speed-to-building-height collision comparison is an illustration rather than a verified universal equivalence and is withheld. [A40]
The shoulder-belt fist-gap fitting instruction needs comparison with current authoritative fitting guidance before learner use; proper routing and lap-belt position are retained. [A41]
The earlier all-children-twelve-and-under rear-seat instruction conflicts with the later under-twelve-and-under-one-hundred-pounds if-possible rule; neither numerical rear-seat mandate is asserted as stable law. [A42] [A43]
The categorical forward-facing instruction at age two lacks manufacturer height/weight context and remains safety verification debt. [A42]
The seat-belt rule uses strictly more than eight years, while the booster rule uses less than eight; the exact-eighth-birthday boundary is unresolved and no bridging rule is invented. [A43]
Confidence process: every drafted fact received a same-model source-context check before submission; independent coverage and hallucination QA remain pending.
Officeholders, telephone numbers and changing administrative details are excluded from stable learner statements. No source attribution is a legal or clinical signoff.
